name: Lamps and Legs
tagline: Flight Console with every lit instrument kept and every code taken out: a jewel for what is on, the live leg lit, each leg's length written over its arc, and plain words beside every lamp.
concept: Flight Console, finished: every lit instrument of Lamps and Ladders kept, and every code the family had to learn replaced by Go's plain words and numbers. The console is slate, steel and Plex; the flight plan is a steel-cyan line whose legs carry their length in days over each arc and whose stops are numbered to the rows; #6dff9c is light on a short list: the mark, one primary, the lit word 'plan', focus, the Now needle and live leg, the jewels, the console clock, and tubes of real curved glass. One readout rail runs the full width of its bay on every page that counts something, each count said once, only Today and Late lit in small windows of glass.
companions: Slate (#111716) for every bay under one 2px top rule. Steel (#6f8596, #a9c4d8 cap) for 'here', today, the family's side of the log and the chat's wire. Steel-cyan (#8fbfdc, flown legs #56707e) only as the flight plan's lines and stop rings. Pewter rings for off and flown. Amber (#e3a651) only for late and needs a look, as a bar, an edge, words, the setup rings or the late window. Clay (#c79071) for restaurants (the swatch and the fork-and-knife in Lately added's head), rust (#d56a53) for the seasonal kind and a grounded straw (#bdb77e) for activities, all three as matte swatches only, so amber alone means late on the desk.
